_README: Route landing pages. Each entry generates one page via:
These exist because 'nice airport to monaco transfer' and similar are how
people actually search. A single destinations page cannot rank for all of
them; a focused page per route can.
Adding a route: copy an entry, change the fields, run the build. It also
rewrites sitemap.xml and the route list on destinations.html.
Keep each page genuinely useful — real journey detail, honest caveats,
route-specific questions. Thin duplicated pages are worse than no pages.
Journey times are estimates in normal traffic, and the pages say so.
The notes on trains and buses are deliberately general: verify current
services before making them more specific.

routes.title: Nice Airport to Monaco Transfer | Private Driver — Mr. Franck
routes.metaDescription: Private transfer from Nice Airport to Monaco with a licensed, English-speaking driver. Around 35–50 minutes, one fixed all-in price agreed before you travel, flight tracked, met inside arrivals.
routes.lead: Around 35 to 50 minutes, door to door, in a car booked for you alone — at a price agreed in writing before you land.
intro: Monaco is close enough to Nice Airport that people assume it's simple. Then they arrive with luggage at eleven at night and discover the principality is a warren of one-way tunnels, underground car parks and addresses that satnavs place on the wrong level.

Franck does this run constantly. He knows which entrance your hotel actually uses, which tunnel to take at the Casino, and that the lift from the Port Hercule car park comes out two streets from where you thought it would.
expect: Met inside the arrivals hall with your name on a sign — not in a car park.
Your flight tracked, so a delay costs nothing and changes nothing.
The A8 autoroute when time matters; the Moyenne Corniche when you'd rather see the coast. Franck will ask.
Dropped at the door — the Hermitage, the Fairmont, Port Hercule, the Casino, or a private address in Fontvieille.
No border formality. Monaco is a separate country, but there is nothing to show and nothing to stop for.
alternatives: Taxi from the rank
Metered, with airport and luggage supplements you learn about at the end. The fare to Monaco is not small, and you will not know it until you arrive.
Tram, then train

Cheap and genuinely scenic. It also means a tram from the airport into Nice-Ville, a wait, a train, and then the long walk up out of Monaco's station with your cases. Fine unencumbered on a sunny afternoon; less so at midnight with a family.
Airport bus
Cheapest of all, and slow. Fixed stops, limited luggage space, and it stops running earlier than most flights land.
Mr. Franck
One fixed price agreed before you travel, tolls and parking included, met inside arrivals, straight to the door. Priced per car, so four of you costs the same as one.
faqs: How long does the transfer from Nice Airport to Monaco really take?

Usually 35 to 50 minutes on the A8. Allow longer on a Friday evening in summer, during the Grand Prix, and whenever the Yacht Show is on — Franck will tell you honestly what to expect for your date rather than quoting the best case.
Do I need my passport to go to Monaco?
Monaco is an independent country, but there is no border control on the road from France. Bring photo ID as you would anywhere, but expect to drive straight in without stopping.
Can you collect us after a late arrival?
Yes. Late flights are routine — send the flight number and Franck tracks it. He would far rather wait than have you stranded at the rank.
Can we stop at Èze on the way?
It's the best detour on this coast and adds roughly an hour. Say so when you book so it's priced in rather than negotiated at the roadside.
What happens during the Monaco Grand Prix?
Large parts of the principality close and access is restricted for days either side. It's still very doable, but it needs planning and it needs booking early — that week sells out months ahead.

routes.title: Nice Airport to Cannes Transfer | Private Driver — Mr. Franck
routes.metaDescription: Private transfer from Nice Airport to Cannes with a licensed, English-speaking driver. Around 30–40 minutes, one fixed all-in price agreed before you travel, flight tracked, met inside arrivals.
routes.lead: Half an hour down the coast, in a car booked for you alone, at a price agreed in writing before you land.
intro: Cannes is the easiest of the major runs from Nice Airport — right up until May, when the Film Festival closes half the Croisette and the traffic on the Bord de Mer stops moving entirely.

The rest of the year it is a straightforward thirty-something minutes. Franck's value is knowing which of those two situations you are actually in, and telling you before you build a schedule around the wrong one.
expect: Met inside the arrivals hall with your name on a sign.
Flight tracked, so a delay costs nothing.
The A8 when the coast road is busy, the Bord de Mer when it isn't and you'd rather look at the sea.
Dropped at the door — the Martinez, the Carlton, the Majestic, the Palais des Festivals, the old port, or a villa above the town.
Help with the bags, which matters more than it sounds on the Croisette in August.
alternatives: Taxi from the rank
Metered, plus supplements. Expect to queue, and expect the fare to be a surprise.
Train
There is a direct rail line along the coast, but not from the airport — you need to get into Nice-Ville or Cannes' own station first, with your luggage, and then out the other end.
Airport bus
A direct coach runs between the airport and Cannes. Reasonable value, fixed stops, limited luggage, and no help at either end.
Mr. Franck
One fixed price, agreed before you travel and including tolls and parking. Met inside arrivals, driven to the door, per car rather than per person.
faqs: How long is the transfer from Nice Airport to Cannes?
Typically 30 to 40 minutes. In the third week of May, during the Film Festival, treat every published journey time as fiction and ask Franck what the day actually looks like.
Can you collect us during the Cannes Film Festival?
Yes, and it's one of his busiest weeks — which is exactly why it needs booking months ahead. Road closures and restricted access around the Palais are planned around, not discovered on the day.
Do you go to Mougins, Mandelieu and Théoule?
Yes. Anywhere around Cannes is straightforward, including the villas up in the hills that satnavs routinely place in the wrong valley.
Can we stop somewhere on the way?
Antibes and Juan-les-Pins are directly en route and make an easy stop. Mention it when you book so the price accounts for it.

routes.title: Nice Airport to Saint-Tropez Transfer | Private Driver — Mr. Franck
routes.metaDescription: Private transfer from Nice Airport to Saint-Tropez with a licensed, English-speaking driver. Around 1h30–2h30 depending on season, one fixed all-in price agreed before you travel.
routes.lead: The long one — and the one where having someone else drive genuinely changes the day.
intro: Saint-Tropez is 115 kilometres from Nice Airport, and the last fifteen of them are the problem. The road into the gulf funnels every car in the region through the same few roundabouts, and in August that final stretch can take longer than the ninety minutes that preceded it.

This is the transfer where a fixed price matters most. On a meter, a summer Friday afternoon into Saint-Tropez is an unpleasant surprise. Agreed in advance, it is simply the price — and the traffic becomes Franck's problem instead of yours.
expect: An honest journey time for your actual date, not the optimistic one.
Flight tracked, met inside arrivals, bags handled.
A comfortable car for what is a proper drive — water, air conditioning, and a stop if you want one.
Dropped at the door in Saint-Tropez, Ramatuelle, Gassin, Pampelonne or Port Grimaud.
The same price whether the road is clear or you spend forty minutes at the gendarmerie roundabout.
alternatives: Hiring a car
Then you own the parking problem, which in Saint-Tropez in season is a genuine one, and nobody in the party can drink at lunch.
Train
Saint-Tropez has no railway station. The nearest is Saint-Raphaël, and you still need to cover the last stretch by road or boat with your luggage.
Boat from Saint-Raphaël or Sainte-Maxime
Lovely in good weather and a real option for a day trip. As an arrival plan with suitcases and a flight time to meet, less so.
Mr. Franck
One car, one fixed price, door to door, with the summer traffic priced in rather than metered.
faqs: How long does it take to get from Nice Airport to Saint-Tropez?

Between an hour and a half and two and a half hours, and occasionally longer. July and August, and Friday and Saturday afternoons in particular, are the slow ones. Franck will tell you what to expect for your date rather than quoting the best case.
Is it cheaper to fly to Toulon or Marseille instead?

Sometimes — Toulon-Hyères is considerably closer to Saint-Tropez than Nice is. If you are still choosing flights, ask Franck before you book; he covers both airports and will tell you honestly which makes more sense.
Can you take us to Pampelonne beach or the villa?
Yes. Ramatuelle, Gassin, Pampelonne and Port Grimaud are all normal drops, including the beach clubs and the addresses down unmarked lanes.
Can we book the return as well?
Yes, and most people do. Same driver, same car, same price agreed in advance — and he will work backwards from your flight to tell you when you actually need to leave.
